title: Heat and Mass Transfer
quiz_title: Quiz 3: Phase Change Heat Transfer & Heat Exchangers

questions.question: Boiling heat transfer occurs when:

options.A: A solid surface is heated below the saturation temperature of a liquid
options.B: A heated surface contacts a liquid at or above its saturation temperature, causing phase change to vapor
options.C: A liquid is cooled below freezing

questions.question: Pool boiling refers to boiling:

options.A: In a flowing stream with forced convection
options.B: In a stationary/quiescent liquid heated by a submerged surface

questions.question: Flow boiling (forced convection boiling) occurs when:

options.A: The liquid is stationary
options.B: The liquid is forced to flow while being heated, causing boiling
options.C: There is no heating at all

questions.question: The boiling curve (Nukiyama curve) plots:

options.A: Heat flux vs excess temperature (ΔTe = Ts − Tsat)
options.B: Pressure vs volume

questions.question: In the boiling curve, the regime before the onset of nucleate boiling is called:

options.A: Natural convection (free convection) boiling regime
options.B: Film boiling regime

questions.question: The regime of pool boiling with the highest heat transfer coefficient is:

options.A: Natural convection boiling
options.B: Nucleate boiling

questions.question: The point on the boiling curve where heat flux is maximum is called:

options.A: Leidenfrost point
options.B: Critical heat flux (CHF) / burnout point

questions.question: The Leidenfrost point refers to:

options.A: The point of maximum heat flux
options.B: The point of minimum heat flux in film boiling (minimum film boiling point)
options.D: The point of zero heat flux

questions.question: In nucleate boiling, bubbles are formed at:

options.A: The bulk liquid only
options.B: Nucleation sites on the heated surface (cavities, scratches)
options.C: Only at the free liquid surface
options.D: Random locations unrelated to the surface

questions.question: Exceeding the critical heat flux in boiling can lead to:

options.A: Improved heat transfer
options.B: Burnout — a sudden rise in surface temperature due to transition to film boiling

questions.question: In film boiling, the heated surface is covered by:

options.A: A liquid film only
options.B: A continuous vapor film that insulates the surface from the liquid

questions.question: Heat transfer in the film boiling regime occurs mainly by:

options.A: Conduction and radiation through the vapor film
options.B: Pure convection in the liquid

questions.question: The Rohsenow correlation is used to predict:

options.A: Condensation heat transfer coefficient
options.B: Nucleate pool boiling heat transfer

questions.question: Zuber's correlation is commonly used to estimate:

options.A: Nucleate boiling heat transfer coefficient
options.B: Critical heat flux in pool boiling

questions.question: Subcooled boiling occurs when:

options.A: The bulk liquid temperature is above the saturation temperature
options.B: The bulk liquid temperature is below saturation while surface temperature exceeds it, causing local boiling
options.C: There is no boiling at all

questions.question: Saturated boiling occurs when:

options.A: The bulk liquid temperature equals the saturation temperature corresponding to system pressure
options.B: The liquid is subcooled
options.C: The liquid is superheated vapor only

questions.question: In flow boiling inside a tube, which regime is typically NOT encountered?

options.A: Bubbly flow
options.B: Slug flow

questions.question: Dryout in flow boiling refers to:

options.A: Complete filling of the tube with liquid
options.B: The liquid film on the tube wall evaporating completely, leaving a dry wall with vapor flow

questions.question: The onset of nucleate boiling (ONB) refers to:

options.A: The point where surface temperature is enough to initiate bubble formation
options.B: The maximum heat flux point
options.C: The minimum heat flux point in film boiling

questions.question: The heat transfer coefficient in nucleate boiling generally depends on:

options.A: Surface roughness, liquid properties, and heat flux/excess temperature
options.B: Only ambient air temperature

questions.question: In pool boiling, increasing surface roughness generally:

options.A: Decreases the number of nucleation sites
options.B: Increases nucleation sites, enhancing nucleate boiling heat transfer

questions.question: Which of these factors influences critical heat flux in pool boiling?

options.A: Surface tension, latent heat of vaporization, and density difference between liquid and vapor
options.B: Only ambient pressure

questions.question: Transition boiling is characterized by:

options.A: A stable, continuous vapor film
options.B: Unstable alternation between nucleate and film boiling, with decreasing heat flux as temperature increases

questions.question: Latent heat of vaporization plays a role in boiling heat transfer because:

options.A: It is the energy absorbed per unit mass during phase change from liquid to vapor
options.B: It has no role
options.D: It is a measure of surface tension

questions.question: Enhancement of boiling heat transfer can be achieved by:

options.A: Using smooth, polished surfaces only
options.B: Using surfaces with engineered nucleation sites/porous coatings to increase bubble nucleation

questions.question: Condensation occurs when a vapor contacts a surface at a temperature:

options.A: Above the saturation temperature
options.B: Below the saturation temperature of the vapor
options.C: Equal to the boiling point of the liquid

questions.question: Film-wise condensation occurs when:

options.A: The condensate does not wet the surface, forming droplets
options.B: The condensate wets the surface, forming a continuous liquid film

questions.question: Drop-wise condensation occurs when:

options.A: Condensate forms a continuous film
options.B: The condensate forms discrete droplets that roll off the surface

questions.question: Compared to film-wise condensation, drop-wise condensation generally gives:

options.A: A lower heat transfer coefficient
options.B: A much higher heat transfer coefficient due to less thermal resistance

questions.question: Nusselt's theory of film condensation assumes:

options.A: Turbulent condensate film flow with significant inertia effects
options.B: Laminar condensate film flow, heat transfer by conduction through the film, negligible inertia/convection effects
options.D: Condensate film at the vapor temperature throughout

questions.question: In Nusselt's theory for condensation on a vertical plate, the condensate film thickness:

options.A: Decreases with distance from the top
options.B: Increases with distance from the top due to continuous condensation

questions.question: The average heat transfer coefficient for laminar film condensation on a vertical plate (Nusselt's theory) is proportional to:

options.A: L (plate length) to a positive power
options.B: L^(−1/4) — inversely related to the fourth root of plate length

questions.question: In Nusselt's theory, the driving temperature difference for condensation is:

options.A: Tsat − Ts (saturation temperature minus surface temperature)
options.B: Ts − T∞ only

questions.question: For condensation on a horizontal tube versus a vertical tube of similar height, generally:

options.A: The horizontal tube gives a higher average heat transfer coefficient
options.B: The vertical tube always gives a higher coefficient
options.D: The horizontal tube gives zero heat transfer

questions.question: Film condensation correlations typically incorporate:

options.A: Only the Reynolds number
options.B: Latent heat, film thickness/geometry, and fluid properties like density, viscosity, thermal conductivity

questions.question: In condensation over a bank of horizontal tubes, the heat transfer coefficient of the lower tubes is generally:

options.A: Higher than the top tube due to drainage from above
options.B: Lower than the top tube because of extra condensate film thickness from drainage
options.C: The same as the top tube

questions.question: The condensate Reynolds number is used to determine:

options.A: Whether the condensate film flow is laminar, wavy-laminar, or turbulent
options.B: Pressure drop in pipes only

questions.question: For laminar film condensation, the condensate Reynolds number is typically:

options.A: Less than about 30 (laminar, wave-free)
options.B: Greater than 10,000

questions.question: As the condensate Reynolds number increases beyond the laminar range, the flow becomes:

options.A: Wavy-laminar and then turbulent, which can enhance heat transfer
options.B: Stopped entirely

questions.question: In practical condenser design, assuming pure vapor (no non-condensable gases) is important because:

options.A: Non-condensable gases accumulate at the surface and can drastically reduce heat transfer
options.B: They have no effect

questions.question: Dropwise condensation is promoted industrially by:

options.A: Roughening the surface
options.B: Applying coatings that reduce wettability (promoters)

questions.question: For film condensation on an inclined plate, the heat transfer coefficient compared to a vertical plate of the same length is generally:

options.A: The same
options.B: Modified by the angle of inclination (typically lower as incline decreases from vertical)

questions.question: Nusselt's theory assumes the vapor is:

options.A: Highly turbulent, interacting significantly with the condensate film
options.B: Stationary/saturated with negligible shear and drag on the condensate film

questions.question: In film condensation analysis, the latent heat of vaporization is often corrected to:

options.A: Account for sensible subcooling of the condensate below saturation temperature (modified latent heat, h'fg)
options.B: Zero, since latent heat has no role

questions.question: For condensation on a vertical tube, the local heat transfer coefficient generally:

options.A: Increases with distance from the top
options.B: Decreases with distance from the top due to increasing film thickness

questions.question: Filmwise condensation is the more common mode in industrial condensers because:

options.A: It is always thermally superior
options.B: Most surfaces are wetted by the condensing liquid and drop-wise condensation is hard to sustain

questions.question: The condensation heat transfer coefficient generally depends on:

options.A: Fluid properties (k, μ, ρ, hfg), surface orientation, temperature difference, and geometry
options.B: Only the color of the surface
options.D: Only the tube material's electrical conductivity

questions.question: For N horizontal tubes stacked vertically, the overall average condensation coefficient is related to the single-tube value by a factor involving:

options.B: N²

questions.question: Which of these is a direct output of Nusselt's film condensation analysis?

options.A: Local condensate film thickness δ(x)
options.B: Pressure drop across a pump

questions.question: In condensation over a vertical plate, the total condensation rate relates to:

options.A: Total heat transferred divided by the modified latent heat of vaporization
options.B: Surface temperature only
options.D: Vapor pressure only, with no energy relation

questions.question: A heat exchanger is a device used to:

options.A: Generate electricity
options.B: Transfer heat between two or more fluids at different temperatures, typically without mixing them

questions.question: Based on flow arrangement, heat exchangers are classified as:

options.A: Parallel flow, counterflow, and cross flow
options.B: Only parallel flow

questions.question: In a parallel flow heat exchanger, the hot and cold fluids:

options.A: Flow in opposite directions
options.B: Flow in the same direction

questions.question: In a counterflow heat exchanger, the hot and cold fluids:

options.A: Flow in the same direction
options.B: Flow in opposite directions

questions.question: In a cross-flow heat exchanger, the fluids:

options.A: Flow parallel to each other
options.B: Flow perpendicular to each other

questions.question: Based on construction, a common heat exchanger type is:

options.A: Shell and tube heat exchanger
options.B: Only plate type

questions.question: A double-pipe heat exchanger consists of:

options.A: Multiple shells with no tubes
options.B: One pipe inside another (concentric tubes), with one fluid in the inner pipe and the other in the annulus

questions.question: In a shell-and-tube heat exchanger, baffles are provided to:

options.A: Reduce heat transfer
options.B: Increase shell-side turbulence and support the tubes, enhancing heat transfer

questions.question: Compact heat exchangers are characterized by:

options.A: Very low surface area to volume ratio
options.B: Very high surface area to volume ratio, suitable for e.g. automobile radiators
options.C: Large physical size with low efficiency

questions.question: Regenerative heat exchangers operate by:

options.A: Continuous flow of both fluids through separate channels only
options.B: Alternately exposing a storage matrix to hot and cold fluid streams, storing and releasing heat

questions.question: Recuperative heat exchangers are characterized by:

options.A: Fluids flowing through separate passages separated by a wall, exchanging heat continuously
options.B: Fluids mixing completely
options.C: No wall ever separating the fluids

questions.question: In a direct contact (open) heat exchanger:

options.A: The two fluids are physically separated by a wall at all times
options.B: The two fluids mix directly with each other to exchange heat

questions.question: The overall heat transfer coefficient U in a heat exchanger accounts for:

options.A: Only convection on the hot side
options.B: Convective resistances on both sides, wall conduction resistance, and fouling resistances

questions.question: Fouling factor (fouling resistance) is added to overall heat transfer coefficient calculations to account for:

options.A: Deposits/scaling on heat exchanger surfaces over time, reducing heat transfer
options.B: Fluid velocity only

questions.question: Overall heat transfer coefficient 1/U for a tube with convection on both sides, wall conduction and fouling is calculated by:

options.A: Summing all individual thermal resistances per unit area, analogous to resistances in series
options.B: Simply adding h_inner and h_outer
options.C: Taking only the smaller h value

questions.question: Fouling in heat exchangers generally leads to:

options.A: Decreased overall heat transfer coefficient and increased pressure drop
options.B: Increased overall heat transfer coefficient

questions.question: In a shell-and-tube exchanger, 'tube passes' refer to:

options.A: The number of times the tube-side fluid traverses the length of the exchanger
options.B: The number of shells only

questions.question: Plate heat exchangers are often preferred over shell-and-tube types because they offer:

options.A: Lower heat transfer area for a given volume
options.B: Compact size, high heat transfer coefficients, and easy cleaning/maintenance
options.C: No ability to handle high pressures ever
options.D: Only single-pass flow, with no flexibility

questions.question: Selecting corrosion- and fouling-resistant materials for heat exchangers is important because it:

options.A: Has no effect on performance
options.B: Maintains heat transfer efficiency and extends equipment life

questions.question: A condenser used in a power plant is a heat exchanger where:

options.A: Both fluids remain single phase, with no phase change
options.B: Steam undergoes condensation (phase change) while cooling water remains single phase

questions.question: An evaporator in a refrigeration system is a heat exchanger where:

options.A: The refrigerant absorbs heat and evaporates, while the other fluid is cooled
options.B: No phase change occurs

questions.question: In heat exchanger terminology, 'single pass' and 'multi-pass' usually refer to:

options.A: The number of times a fluid flows through the exchanger's tube or shell side
options.B: The type of fluid used

questions.question: A primary advantage of using multiple tube passes in a shell-and-tube exchanger is:

options.A: Increased fluid velocity and heat transfer coefficient for a given tube-side flow rate
options.B: Decreased heat transfer area

questions.question: A plate-fin heat exchanger is commonly used in applications requiring:

options.A: Large, bulky equipment with low heat transfer per unit volume
options.B: Compact, lightweight design with high heat transfer efficiency, e.g. aerospace and cryogenics
options.C: Only liquid-liquid heat transfer at low temperatures

questions.question: Thermal resistance due to the tube wall in overall heat transfer coefficient calculations is generally significant when:

options.A: The wall is very thin and made of a highly conductive material
options.B: The wall material has low thermal conductivity or is relatively thick
options.D: Only fouling matters; wall resistance is always negligible

questions.question: LMTD stands for:

options.A: Linear Mean Temperature Difference
options.B: Logarithmic Mean Temperature Difference

questions.question: LMTD is used primarily to calculate:

options.A: The pressure drop in heat exchangers
options.B: The effective average temperature difference driving heat transfer in a heat exchanger

questions.question: The formula for LMTD is:

options.A: (ΔT1 − ΔT2) / ln(ΔT1/ΔT2)

questions.question: For the same inlet and outlet temperatures, counterflow heat exchangers generally have:

options.A: A lower LMTD than parallel flow
options.B: A higher LMTD than parallel flow, making them more effective
options.C: The same LMTD as parallel flow always

questions.question: In a parallel flow heat exchanger, the outlet temperature of the cold fluid can never:

options.A: Be lower than the inlet temperature of the hot fluid
options.B: Exceed the outlet temperature of the hot fluid
options.C: Equal the inlet temperature of the cold fluid

questions.question: In a counterflow heat exchanger, the outlet temperature of the cold fluid CAN:

options.A: Never exceed the inlet temperature of the hot fluid
options.B: Exceed the outlet temperature of the hot fluid (but not the hot fluid's inlet)
options.D: Always equal the hot fluid's inlet temperature

questions.question: The correction factor F is applied to LMTD for:

options.A: Simple double-pipe counterflow only
options.B: Complex flow arrangements like shell-and-tube with multiple passes or cross-flow

questions.question: The correction factor F for LMTD is always:

options.A: Greater than 1
options.B: Less than or equal to 1

questions.question: When one fluid undergoes phase change (condensation or evaporation) at constant temperature, the LMTD calculation:

options.A: Cannot be used at all
options.B: Still applies, treating that fluid's temperature as constant throughout

questions.question: The LMTD method is best suited for problems where:

options.A: Inlet and outlet temperatures of both fluids are known, and the heat exchanger size is to be determined
options.B: Fluid properties are unknown
options.C: Exit temperatures and flow rates are both unknown
options.D: Pressure drop is being studied, not temperature

questions.question: The effectiveness-NTU (ε-NTU) method is particularly useful when:

options.A: All four terminal temperatures are known (the easy case for LMTD)
options.B: One or more exit temperatures are unknown, which would otherwise need iterative LMTD solutions
options.C: There is no need to evaluate heat exchanger performance
options.D: The heat exchanger is a direct contact type only

questions.question: Effectiveness (ε) of a heat exchanger is defined as:

options.A: The ratio of actual heat transfer rate to the maximum possible heat transfer rate
options.B: The ratio of hot fluid flow rate to cold fluid flow rate

questions.question: NTU stands for:

options.A: Number of Transfer Units
options.B: Net Thermal Utilization

questions.question: NTU is defined as:

options.A: UA / C_min (overall conductance divided by minimum heat capacity rate)
options.B: U / A only

questions.question: The heat capacity rate ratio 'Cr' used in effectiveness-NTU relations is defined as:

options.A: C_min / C_max
options.B: C_max / C_min

questions.question: The maximum possible heat transfer rate (Q_max) in a heat exchanger is given by:

options.A: C_min × (T_hot,in − T_cold,in)
options.B: C_max × (T_hot,in − T_cold,in)

questions.question: For a counterflow heat exchanger with Cr = 1 (equal heat capacity rates), the effectiveness is given by:

options.A: ε = NTU/(1+NTU)
options.B: ε = 1 − e^(−NTU)

questions.question: For a condenser or evaporator where one fluid undergoes phase change, Cr (C_min/C_max) approaches:

options.B: Infinity
options.C: 0, since the phase-changing fluid has effectively infinite heat capacity rate

questions.question: For the Cr = 0 case, the effectiveness relation for any flow arrangement simplifies to:

options.A: ε = 1 − e^(−NTU)
options.B: ε = NTU/(1+NTU)

questions.question: Increasing the NTU of a heat exchanger (e.g. by increasing area) generally:

options.A: Decreases effectiveness
options.B: Increases effectiveness up to an asymptotic maximum

questions.question: The effectiveness-NTU method is advantageous for performance/rating problems because it:

options.A: Requires iterative trial and error always, like LMTD
options.B: Allows direct calculation of effectiveness and heat transfer without iteration when NTU and Cr are known
options.C: Cannot be used for design purposes

questions.question: In the LMTD method, when both exit temperatures are unknown, the typical solution approach is:

options.A: A direct single-step calculation
options.B: An iterative (trial and error) procedure assuming exit temperatures, computing LMTD, and refining
options.D: Use of the Nusselt number directly

questions.question: The relationship connecting LMTD, overall heat transfer coefficient, and heat transfer area to total heat transfer rate is:

options.A: Q = U·A·LMTD
options.B: Q = U/A·LMTD

questions.question: For a given heat exchanger with fixed NTU and flow arrangement, a counterflow configuration generally provides:

options.A: Lower effectiveness than parallel flow
options.B: Higher (or equal) effectiveness compared to parallel flow for the same NTU and Cr
options.C: The same performance as an adiabatic system

questions.question: Both the LMTD and ε-NTU methods are ultimately based on:

options.A: Completely different, unrelated fundamental principles
options.B: The same fundamental energy balance and rate equations for heat exchangers, approached differently
options.C: Only empirical correlations with no theoretical basis
